capabilities.name: Strategic direction
capabilities.question: Which objectives do we pursue, and what do they mean for technology?

capabilities.name: Investment & funding
capabilities.question: How much money flows where, and within which guardrails?
capabilities.leadNote: EPM leads across the enterprise (portfolio budgets, guardrails, cross-portfolio investments); LPM then takes the lead within each portfolio (value stream funding). In the compact variant without a separate EPM level, LPM or an integrated portfolio governance leads throughout.

capabilities.name: Prioritisation & dependencies
capabilities.question: What do we do first, what not at all, and what depends on what?

capabilities.name: Cost transparency & allocation
capabilities.question: What does technology cost, for what, and who consumes it?

capabilities.name: Architecture & lifecycle
capabilities.question: Which target architecture, which technology is ending, which risks exist?

capabilities.name: Delivery & capacity
capabilities.question: How does work flow through limited capacity?

capabilities.name: Operations & service quality
capabilities.question: Do services run reliably, securely and economically?

capabilities.name: Value realisation & reallocation
capabilities.question: Does it work? What do we keep funding, change or stop?

environment.name: Corporate finance processes
environment.description: Budgeting, forecasting, accounting and capitalisation – adjacent to technology steering, not part of TBM.

links.label: Objectives and investment themes set the direction for funding.
Approved budgets and guardrails define what can be prioritised.
Prioritised investments are pulled into delivery.
Delivered products and changes go into operation.
Usage, service quality and run cost show what is actually achieved.
Realised outcomes revise objectives and themes.
Results trigger continued funding, reallocation or stop.
Actual and forecast cost by solution and consumer inform budgets.
Allocated actual cost shows the economics of what was delivered.
Run cost and consumption drivers flow into cost allocation.
Dependencies and end-of-life dates constrain sequencing.
Target architecture and platforms shape how work is delivered.
Capability map and technology risk inform strategic choices.
Budgeting and forecasting provide the financial frame.
Accounting delivers booked actuals to the cost model.
